# Field Shift

> A field-first crop rotation planner that combines NASA POWER climate records with a farmer's current crop and local priorities.

Field Shift is decision support for farmers and agricultural extension workers. It compares rotation options using transparent, rule-based scores and explains the climate evidence, benefits, and risks. It does not predict yield or replace local agronomic advice, soil tests, or field observation. NASA does not endorse the rotation scores.

## Product

- Home: https://fieldshift.cloud/
- Open the rotation explorer: https://fieldshift.cloud/explorer/
- User guide: https://fieldshift.cloud/explorer/User_guide
- About: https://fieldshift.cloud/explorer/About
- Data sources: https://fieldshift.cloud/explorer/Data_sources
- Privacy: https://fieldshift.cloud/explorer/Privacy
- Disclaimer: https://fieldshift.cloud/explorer/Disclaimer

## Data and method

- Climate comes from NASA POWER daily point data for the selected field coordinates.
- Inputs include location, current crop, soil context, climate period, and farmer priorities.
- Scores compare water resilience, soil-health potential, and priority match. They are not yield estimates.
- Place search and map naming use OpenStreetMap Nominatim. Map tiles and geographic names are attributed in the app.
- Source and licensing details: https://fieldshift.cloud/explorer/Data_sources

## Privacy and limits

- On the hosted service, saved field records and cached climate files are stored on the machine operated for fieldshift.cloud. The app has no user account system or self-service deletion control.
- Coordinates are sent to NASA POWER for climate requests. Place search text or coordinates may be sent to OpenStreetMap Nominatim.
- Do not enter confidential personal information. Read the privacy notice for storage and deletion details.
- There is no field-level yield, soil-moisture, market-price, or irrigation dataset in this build.
